Chapter One: The World Before Change—Old Powers and Everyday Struggles
Picture this—you're standing in the heart of a bustling city square. People from every background brush past you. Some move with confidence, dressed in fine clothes, their words carrying real weight. Others keep to the sidelines, faces etched with years of hard work and quiet worry.
In this world, the rules? They’ve been set long before any of us were born. A lucky few inherit titles and lands, while the rest are left to get by with whatever they can. There’s this heavy feeling in the air, like things have always been this way... and maybe always will be.
For generations, families have watched power handed down from father to son—not because of wisdom or kindness, but simply because of bloodlines. The king’s word? It’s law. And those who serve him—the lords, the dukes, all the nobles—enjoy perks that seem almost magical if you’re not part of their world. Meanwhile, most folks—farmers, shopkeepers, artisans—shoulder the weight of endless taxes and duties. Their voices? Barely a whisper in the grand halls where decisions get made.
In the quiet corners of their homes, parents tell their kids to keep their heads down and accept their place. Sure, some dream of something more, but most learn pretty early on: if you question the way things are, you’re only asking for trouble. The idea that everyone should have a say in how they’re governed? It feels about as close as the stars.
Still, underneath it all, you can sense frustration simmering. Maybe it’s a merchant, who’s spent years working hard, only to watch his earnings vanish into taxes that fund the lavish lives of the elite. Or a young woman, smart and capable, but shut out of opportunities just because of her family name. Even some who serve the king start to wonder—why is their loyalty rewarded with so little, when others get so much just by being born into the right family?
Every now and then, whispers of change float in from faraway places. Stories of ordinary people rising up, demanding fairness, claiming rights that once seemed impossible. These tales light a spark—hope for some, fear for others. The old guard insists tradition is sacred, that without monarchy and inherited rule, the world would just fall apart. But for many, that question hangs in the air: does it really have to be this way?
Back then, the idea of rights—something every person deserves just for being human—was almost unthinkable. Most people accepted that their lives were shaped by forces they couldn’t control. But as the years dragged on, and the burdens got heavier, more and more folks started to wonder if things could change. Maybe, just maybe, the world didn’t have to run on old power and privilege forever.
